program.name: ndm_detectspikes
program.help:
Detect spikes on a high-pass filtered .fil file and write the shared spike-time .res files.
First, the program automatically computes a baseline 'noise' level, using a subset of the data. Then, spikes are detected whenever the signal crosses a threshold proportional to the baseline 'noise' level. To avoid spurious detections, the signal must have a local maximum (or minimum, depending on the sign of the signal) within a fixed search window starting at threshold crossing. Also, the duration between consecutive spikes must be greater than a fixed 'refractory' period.
The detection engine (method: standard, sdiff, or stderiv) and, for sdiff/stderiv, the spatial-derivative order (methodOrder) are set in the session's ndm_detectspikes program node; they are not declared here. The detection engine also produces a .spk in passing (there is no detect-only engine mode), which is discarded — ndm_extractspikes produces the waveform files from the shared .res.
PARAMETERS
# thresholdFactor
Threshold = thresholdFactor * baseline 'noise' level
# refractoryPeriod
Number of samples to skip after a spike, before trying to detect a new spike
# peakSearchLength
Length of the peak search window (in number of samples)
# start
Starting point in the file (in s) for computation of baseline 'noise' level
# duration
Duration (in s) for computation of baseline 'noise' level
# inputExtension
Extension of the data file read for detection, without the leading dot (default fil, i.e. <session>.fil). Set it to an alternative, externally-processed source (e.g. car.fil or filtered.dat) to detect from that file instead. The source must be high-pass filtered like the usual .fil; ndm_detectspikes does not filter it.
METHOD TOKENS
The method may be qualified so the transform is stated in the artifact name rather than inferred: stderiv_S<order> runs the plain spatial derivative (orders 1-3) and leaves any per-group sdiffPairs unused, while stderiv_C<order> applies the session's sdiffPairs pattern -- order 4 for a single-partner pattern, order 5 for a reference-set pattern (one written with '+'). Outputs are stamped with the full token, e.g. <session>.spk.stderiv_C4.<group>.
Orders 4 and 5 are derived from the pattern itself and cannot be requested through methodOrder; a plain "stderiv" keeps the historical behaviour of applying whatever sdiffPairs the groups define.
